entry.title: Access status checked 30 Oct 2026, 05:14 UTC, after the check of 24 Oct, 05:12 UTC (no check in between): signups open, no new-user credit, API operational; the status page's history lists no incident dated 15–30 Oct. jev-latest and jev-preview still give jev-1.14.0; jev-1.13.0 is still listed with no deprecation date; price unchanged. Three notices, none added or retired.

Decision-API comparison and alternatives: OpenAI's data-controls page now marks the Decisions API eligible for Private Retention and Safety Retention (between 13 and 30 Oct); Microsoft lists regions for Microsoft-Decision-1 (page dated 19 Oct, first seen 30 Oct); SubQ's docs list SubQ Snap 1.1 at $0.04 per million input tokens, output free (between 14 and 28 Oct; the launch post still says $0.05). Unchanged cells re-dated 30 Oct.

Alternatives, Drex row: on 30 Oct 2026, 05:19 UTC Nace.AI's pricing docs list drex-max at $0.03 per 1M input tokens (was $0.06 on 20 Oct), a new drex-max-v1.1 at $0.03, drex-v2.0 $0.06, drex-v1.5 $0.05 and a signup balance of $5.00. Changed between 20 and 30 Oct 2026; the page shows no date. The 20 Oct values are kept as dated.

Versions and aliases and where to use: six route listings rechecked 30 Oct 2026, 05:17 UTC and unchanged (Opper's typesafe/jev-latest still maps to jev-1.13.0). Jev is not listed in the Amazon Bedrock pages, Microsoft Learn's Foundry pages or the Workers AI models page at 30 Oct, 05:17 UTC; the Azure AI Foundry catalog page could not be read and keeps its 16 Oct date.

Errors and rate limits: TypeSafe's models page now takes requests for higher limits through a rate limit increase request form instead of a sales email (changed between 24 Oct, 05:12 UTC and 30 Oct, 05:14 UTC). Limits are still set per organization and shown in the developer console.

Coding agents: acmelabs-15/jev-gate, a Claude Code hook, read in source at a 20 Oct commit: it lets the tool call go ahead when Jev errors, times out after 1.5 seconds, answers malformed or has no key, and by default only logs. Not settled and not on the failure map (still 80). 28 read in source: 14 act on Jev's answer, 10 do not, 4 not settled. Lead triage for 21–30 Oct: ten names classed from their READMEs.

Version notes: ohmyjev 0.13.2 (29 Oct) removes the auto-approve thresholds from its policy file (its failure-map row was read at an earlier version and has not been re-read); auto-mode 3.1.5 shows no change in the files compared; newer versions of @effect/ai-typesafe, pydantic-ai-slim and nace-sdk exist, not re-read; TypeSafe's SDKs unchanged.

New dated report: what changed for Jev builders between the checks of 24 and 30 October 2026, with what was rechecked and unchanged, what changed and since when, which catalogs list Jev, the coding-agent read, the dates the scan covered and the surfaces whose coverage is unknown.

Versions and aliases: jev-latest on TypeSafe's API now gives jev-1.14.0 (first seen 24 Oct 2026, 05:12 UTC; jev-1.13.0 at 23 Oct, 05:45 UTC; no dated announcement); jev-1.13.0 is still listed by its ID with no deprecation date. Opper's typesafe/jev-latest still gave 1.13 that morning. Title without "preview"; six-route table. Pages that name a default model now say what an unpinned request gets.

Benchmarks: new section on the four decision leaderboards that list Jev (Jev Decision Index, Artificial Analysis Decision Index, JevMan, JevBench): who runs each, what you can check, and Jev's listed position. Base Labs' "#1 of 208" claim matches the Jev Decision Index's 20 Oct data, not its 22 Oct data. Leaderboards are not graded.

Benchmarks: four studies graded (B45 and B46 grade A, B47 and B48 grade C); the ledger has 45 graded rows: A 14, B 14, C 10, D 7. Five grade-A comparisons of Jev with OpenAI's Decisions API differ by task, with no overall direction. Same grades on alternatives, the decision-API comparison and reranking and RAG.

Decision-API comparison and alternatives: since general availability OpenAI's Decisions API discounts cached input ($0.01 per 1M tokens) and charges cache writes ($0.125 or $0.25 per 1M); input $0.10 and free output unchanged. The 13 Oct beta wording is kept as dated.
New dated report: jev-latest now gives Jev 1.14; decision leaderboards and four new graded studies (24 Oct 2026).

Access status rechecked 24 Oct 2026, 05:12 UTC: signups open, no new-user credit, API operational; price and rate-limit wording unchanged. On TypeSafe's API jev-latest now points to jev-1.14.0 (first seen 05:12 UTC; it pointed to jev-1.13.0 on 23 Oct); jev-1.13.0 is still listed by its ID, with no deprecation date. Home adds a notice for the move (three notices); none retired.

Limitations: new section "Jev with images". Of 8 SDKs and integrations read in package files, 5 send images to Jev and 2 of those add TypeSafe's opt-in header for you; pydantic-ai refuses images and both LangChain packages pass them as text. TypeSafe's image docs quoted with times; no image was sent.

n8n: TypeSafe's node 0.10.0 keeps the same failure behaviour and adds an Images field that sends PNG or JPEG with the opt-in header. Image lines also on TypeScript, Python, frameworks (pydantic-ai-slim 2.60.0 still refuses images) and errors and limits.

Versions and aliases: sentences that described the jev-latest move as upcoming now give its state on 23 Oct (still jev-1.13.0, no date published). All six routes list a Jev 1.14 ID; a versioned ID can be written on 6 of 6 routes for 1.14 and 5 of 6 for 1.13. Route image fields re-read.

Decision-API comparison and alternatives: OpenAI's Decisions API became generally available on 22 Oct 2026; same model and input price; up to 400 questions per request (200 in the beta). Not re-graded.
When Jev fails and coding agents: the pinned jev-gateway links now point to the repository named in its npm record, at the same commit; cells unchanged.
New dated report: Jev with images, what 8 SDKs and integrations do with an image, and the route counts for Jev 1.14 (23 Oct 2026).
